1.title: Catch-up: Finish Lesson 1
1.text: No new lesson today. We make your multiplying slip-proof: right rows, every column lined up, rows added carefully. 💪

notes.do: Graph paper, pencil, whiteboard and two marker colors. Look at any Graph Paper Practice, packet pages and index card he brought. Note what is missing.
notes.say: Your method is right. Every answer on Friday was close. Today we hunt down the small slips, so close becomes correct.
notes.ask: What did you finish this week? Show me your paper work.
notes.listen: Which pages are done. He should know Lesson 2 is still locked until 85.

7.title: Find the slip
7.text: These are the four you missed on Friday. Your setup was right every time. Work each one on graph paper, find the one slip, then type the right answer.

items.q: You chose 125 and 900 for 45 × 23. What is 45 × 3?
items.why: 5 × 3 = 15: write 5, regroup 1. 4 × 3 = 12, plus the regrouped 1 makes 13. 135.
items.no: Multiply the ones first: 5 × 3 = 15. Write 5, regroup 1.

items.why: 135 + 900 = 1,035. Estimate: 50 × 20 = 1,000. Close, so it is the right size.
67 × 4 = 268 and 67 × 20 = 1,340. 268 + 1,340 = 1,608. The slip was in adding the hundreds.
items.no: Rows: 67 × 4 and 67 × 20. Add one column at a time.

items.q: You typed 1,350 on Oct 26 and 1,630 on Friday. 135 × 12 = ____
items.why: 135 × 2 = 270 and 135 × 10 = 1,350. 270 + 1,350 = 1,620. 1,350 was only one row; 1,630 was a slip in the tens column.
items.no: There are two rows: 135 × 2 and 135 × 10. Add both.

notes.do: He works each one on graph paper, one digit per square, regrouped digits in the second color. Before he types, he says which step slipped: ones row, regroup, or adding the rows.
notes.say: Your setup was right on all four. The points were lost in one small step each time.
notes.ask: Which step slipped? How would you catch it next time?
notes.listen: 135 (the regrouped 1 was dropped), 1,035, 1,608, 476, 1,620. Adding the rows is his most common slip: add one column at a time, ones first.

18.title: Three in a row
18.text: On your own. Estimate, stack it on graph paper, add one column at a time, then type. Get all three right before the retake.

items.no: Ones row: 39 × 6. Tens row: write the 0, then 39 × 2.
Ones row: 58 × 4. Tens row: write the 0, then 58 × 3.
Ones row: 146 × 3. Tens row: write the 0, then 146 × 2.

notes.do: Hands off. He works alone on graph paper and types. Note his first answers. All three right means he retakes Show What You Know now; a miss means one more problem with you first.
